title: Secure Communication Protocols
subtitle: SSH, JWT signing, and secure API authentication

content.text: SSH uses public-key cryptography for authentication and symmetric encryption for the session. Use Ed25519 keys instead of RSA for new setups.

content.code:
# Generate Ed25519 SSH key
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your@email.com"

# View public key to copy to server
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

# Secure SSH config
# /etc/ssh/sshd_config
PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
AllowUsers youruser

content.text: JSON Web Tokens should be signed with RS256 (asymmetric) or HS256 (symmetric HMAC). Asymmetric signing lets any service verify tokens without the secret.

content.code:
import jwt  # pip install pyjwt
import datetime

# HS256 (symmetric)
payload = {"sub": "user123", "exp": datetime.datetime.utcnow() + datetime.timedelta(hours=1)}
token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret_key", algorithm="HS256")
decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret_key", algorithms=["HS256"])

questions.question: Why should you disable PasswordAuthentication in SSH?
options: Passwords are vulnerable to brute force; key-based auth uses unforgeable cryptographic proofs
Key auth is free but password auth costs money
questions.explanation: SSH keys cannot be brute-forced (the private key never crosses the network). Disabling password auth eliminates that attack surface.

faq.q: What algorithm should I use to sign JWTs in production?
faq.a: RS256 (RSA) or ES256 (ECDSA) for services where multiple parties verify tokens. HS256 for a single service that both signs and verifies.
